items.title: Ibn Baṭṭūṭa
items.note: Reference survey of the traveller and the Riḥla, summarising the debate over borrowed passages and doubtful legs.

items.title: Deviser les merveilles du monde
items.note: Rereads the Mali journey within the jointly authored work's literary design built around marvels and the spread of Islam.

items.title: KITAB: Knowledge, Information Technology, and the Arabic Book
items.note: ERC grant of about €1.99 million (2018 to 2023) that adapted passim for Arabic and produced text-reuse data across the OpenITI corpus.

items.title: Ibn Baṭṭūṭa's Buddhists: Monuments, Memory, and the Materiality of Travel
items.venue: Encountering Buddhism and Islam in Premodern Central and South Asia (De Gruyter)
items.note: Examines the Chinese embassy to Delhi that Ibn Baṭṭūṭa was sent to escort, setting his account against monuments and other evidence.

items.title: Ibn Juzayy, Abū ʿAbdallāh
items.note: Entry on the Granadan scholar who wrote up the Riḥla, relevant to which parts reflect his editing and borrowing.

items.title: At the Edge of the World of Islam: Ibn Baṭṭūṭa in the Malay Archipelago
items.note: Analyses the narrative techniques of the Sumatra and archipelago sections of the 1340s and what they reveal about early Islamisation.

items.title: "Le voyageur des Arabes et des Persans": une approche cognitive de la riḥla d'Ibn Baṭṭūṭa (1325-1355)
items.note: Questions the 'great explorer' reading of the Riḥla and treats it as a construction of knowledge about the Islamic world.

items.title: Ibn Baṭṭūṭa's "Prayer of Damascus:" A window on to Damascus in the hell of the Black Death (Part 1)
items.note: Compares the Riḥla's account of the 1348 plague procession in Damascus with Arabic chronicles of the same event.

items.title: Two-year Journey under the Arrows of the Black Death
items.venue: Journal of Arabic and Islamic Studies
items.note: Tests the 1348 to 1350 return journey against plague chronicles and asks whether its plague passages were taken from other sources.

items.title: India's epidemics in the Riḥla of Ibn Baṭṭūṭa: plague, cholera or lexical muddle?
items.venue: Bulletin of the School of Oriental and African Studies
items.note: Checks the Riḥla's Indian epidemics of 1334–35 and 1344 against Indo-Persian chronicles and translations, finding errors introduced by translators.

items.title: The Colonial Adventures of Confiscated Arabic Texts: Ibn Battuta's Rihla Manuscript from North Africa to the French National Library
items.who: S. Ahmed, T. Dumothier and K. M. McGinn
items.note: Uses French archival sources to reconstruct how the Paris manuscripts, including the copy believed to be Ibn Juzayy's, left North Africa.

items.title: KITAB Text Reuse Data, version 2023.1.8
items.who: D. Smith, S. B. Savant, M. Romanov et al.
items.note: Passim alignments across an OpenITI release, the kind of corpus-wide reuse output from which Riḥla parallels can be extracted.

items.title: Princess Urduja From Tawalisi: Arabic Mirabilia And Philippine History
items.note: Reads Tawālisī, a land known only from the Riḥla, as Arabic mirabilia and traces how Philippine historiography adopted it.

items.title: OpenITI: a Machine-Readable Corpus of Islamicate Texts; Primary Version 2025.1.9
items.who: L. Nigst, M. Romanov, S. B. Savant et al.
items.note: Current versioned release of the corpus holding digital witnesses of the Riḥlas of Ibn Baṭṭūṭa and Ibn Jubayr.

items.title: Ibn Baṭṭūṭa's Calicut: An Archaeological Investigation Through Ibn Baṭṭūṭa's and Other Historical Accounts
items.who: M. Shokoohy and N. H. Shokoohy
items.venue: Faith, Commerce, and Cultural Exchange in the World of Ibn Battuta (Springer), ed. A. Panakkal
items.note: Sets the Riḥla's description of Calicut against surviving buildings and other accounts, in a 2026 volume of regional case studies.

items.title: Manuscript of the first part of the Riḥla sold at the Abu Dhabi International Book Fair
items.note: Press report of a sale for close to Dh1 million of a copy covering the journeys of 1325 to 1333; its date and new location are not stated.
